headline: Recommended approval of a fence at 15 Windswept Road within a wetland setback.
summary: Members recommended approval of a variance for a 6-foot white vinyl fence at 15 Windswept Road, which would sit within a wetland. They also approved changing meeting dates to the fourth Wednesday of each month and approved two sets of minutes.
decisions: Recommended approval of a variance for a fence at 15 Windswept Road within a wetland; passed with all in favor.
Approved a request that City Staff write a letter of support for 15 Windswept Road if DES asks for one; passed with all in favor.
Approved changing meeting dates to the fourth Wednesday of each month; passed with all in favor.
Approved June 10, 2026 meeting minutes, with six in favor and one abstention.
Approved June 25, 2026 meeting minutes; passed with all in favor.
Approved a motion to notify NH DES of earlier impact by builders on Map 822 Lot 2E; passed with all in favor.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Zielinski moves that the Conservation Commission support the approval of this application by the Zoning Board of Adjustment ... Commissioner Kaligandis seconds the motion. The motion passes with all in favor.

Commissioner Zielinski moves to request that City Staff write a letter of support on the applicant’s behalf, if requested by DES. Commissioner Boucher seconds the motion. The motion passes with all in favor.
Commissioner Zielinski moves to change the Conservation Commission meeting dates to the fourth Wednesday of each month. Commissioner Boucher seconds the motion. The motion passes with all in favor.

June 10, 2026 meeting minutes are reviewed. Commissioner MacLaren moves to approve the meeting minutes. Commissioner Boucher seconds the motion. Motion passes with six in favor (Commissioners MacLaren, Boucher, Akinci, Kaligandis, Palangas, and Zielinski) and one abstention (Chair Waldron).
June 25, 2026 meeting minutes are reviewed. Commissioner Zielinski moves to approve the meeting minutes. Commissioner MacLaren seconds the motion. The motion passes with all in favor.

Commissioner Palangas moves to notify NH DES that there has been impact previously by the builders, according to a plan prepared by J.E. Belanger Land Surveyors for Map 822 Lot 2E, stamped, dated October 6, 2015. Commissioner Akinci seconds the motion. The motion passes with all in favor.

plain_text:
MANCHESTER CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
c/o City of Manchester Planning and Community Development Department 
One City Hall Plaza 
Manchester, NH 03101 
(603) 624-6450 
pcd@manchesternh.gov 
 
  
MINUTES 
of the 
MANCHESTER CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
 
July 23, 2026 – 6:00 PM 
Walter Stiles Room 
2nd Floor 
Manchester City Hall 
One City Hall Plaza 
 
Commission Members Present: Donald Waldron, Chair 
     Sue Boucher, Vice Chair 
     John Kaligandis  
Jennifer MacLaren 
Thomas Palangas 
     Lauren Zielinski 
     Levent Akinci, Alternate  
 
Commission Members Absent: None 
 
Staff Present:    Kristin Bixby, Senior Planner  
 
 
I. Call to Order 
 
The meeting was called to order at 6:00 PM by Chair Waldron. 
 
II. Roll 
 
Six members and one alternate member  of the Commission are present, constituting a quorum.  
Commissioner Akinci is promoted to a full voting member. 
 
III. Presentation by Stephanie and Aaron Theriault for property located at 15 Windswep t 
Road (Tax Map 822, Lot 2B) , r egarding a variance application (ZBA2026- 070) in 
front of the Manchester Zoning Board of Adjustment to construct a fence within the 
required no disturbance buffer and structural setback from a wetland. 
Stephanie and Aaron Theriault, property owners, are present to discuss the project.   
 
Mr. Theriault explains that their old er son is autistic . A fence is proposed for their son’ s safety. 
They have spoken with all of their neighbors regarding the proposed variance and they support  the 
proposal. None believe t his will infringe on their property values. The fence is proposed to be 
located within the wetland.  A neighbor has stated that he has never seen water up to the gully line 
of the wetland area. It is believed that the g ully was manmade. The plan is for a gate  to lead from
Page | 2  
 
the garage, strai ght back on the property. There is an existing metal chain-link fence in the 
backyard behind the shed for privacy from the highway. The wetland delineation was completed 
when the house was built in 2015. The proposed fence is a 6’ white vinyl fence.  
 
The Commission discusses that the wetlands delineation previously completed may not reflect the 
existing conditions on the site. 
 
Commissioner Zielinski moves t hat the Conservation Commission support the approval of this 
application by the Zoning Board of Adjustment due to the following reasons : that the wetlands 
delineation does not reflect current gradations and wetland conditions, and that there will likely  be 
no impacts to wetlands in the proposed location of the fence. Commissioner Kaligandis seconds the 
motion. The motion passes with all in favor. 
 
Ms. Bixby notes that, until the land has been redelineated, the applicant may need to speak to DES 
about putting the structure within the wetlands. The ZBA can only allow for the  structure to be 
within the wetland  setback. The Commission agree s that Staff could write a let ter of support to 
DES, if needed.  
 
Commissioner Zielinski moves to request that City Staff write a letter of support on the applicant’s 
behalf, if requested by DE S. Commissioner Boucher seconds the motion. The motion passes with 
all in favor. 
 
IV. Discussion on Conservation Commission outreach initiatives. 
The Commission discusses a tour with T he Nature Conservancy (TNC) and potentially dela ying 
this until next year or holding its own tour with printed materials.  
 
Commissioner MacLaren offered to reach out to Parks and Recreation  about the Valley Cemetery 
Tour. There was some discussion on the best person to contact, and the City’s new Urban Forester. 
 
The Commission discusses helping to promote its work at a Community Day on Friday, August 21, 
from 3 PM to 6 PM at Sweeney Park. 
 
V. Discussion on changing Conservation Commission meeting s to the fourth Wednesday 
of each month. 
The Commission agrees to change its meeting to the fourth Wednesday of each month. 
Commissioner Zielinski moves to change the Conservation Commission meeting dates to the 
fourth Wednesday of each month. Commissioner Boucher seconds the motion. The motion passes 
with all in favor. 
 
VI. Review of prior meeting minutes.  
June 10, 2026 meeting minutes are reviewed. Commissioner MacLaren  moves to approve the 
meeting minutes . Commissioner Boucher seconds the motion. Motion passes with six  in favor 
(Commissioners MacLaren, Boucher, Akinci, Kaligandis, Palangas, and Zielinski)  and one 
abstention (Chair Waldron). 
June 25, 2026 meeting minutes are reviewed. Commissioner Zielinski moves to approve the 
meeting minutes . Commissioner MacLaren seconds the motion. The motion passes with all in 
favor.
Page | 3  
 
VII. Staff Update. 
 
Ms. Bixby reviews the new boundary for the easement the Commission agreed to take on as a third 
party. This is the Environmental  Protection Division’s new easement to start a water entrance to a 
new separate stormwater tunnel.  
 
Ms. Bixby states that she has been in conta ct with the Southeast Land T rust of New Hampshire 
(SELT) and they are prepared  to come t o one of the foll owing meetings along with Manchester 
Waterworks for the final drafting of that easement language. 
 
The Commission agreed to meet next on August 19, 2026, pending formal confirmation from the 
City Clerk. 
 
VIII. Other business.  
 
Commissioner Palangas moves to notify NH  DES that there has been impact previously by the  
builders, according to a plan prepared by J.E. Belanger  Land Surveyors for Map  822 Lot 2E , 
stamped, dated October 6, 2015. Commissioner Akinci seconds the motion. The motion passes 
with all in favor. 
 
Chair Waldron notes that this will be his last Commiss ion meeting. The Commission thanks him 
for his work and efforts over the years. 
 
IX. Adjournment 
 
A motion to adjourn was made by Commissioner Akinci , seconded by Chair Waldron. The motion 
passes with all in favor. The meeting is adjourned at 7:02 PM. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
ATTEST:   
Susan Boucher 
                 Chair, Manchester Conservation Commission 
 
 
APPROVED BY THE MANCHESTER CONSERVATION COMMISSION: August 19, 2026 
 
 
 
 
Minutes prepared by: Kristan Patenaude, Recording Secretary
